clue.text: Old officer to give a little extra to those who serve

parts.note: to tip is to give a waiter a little extra money

explanation.surface: A suggestion that an old-fashioned official should leave a gratuity for the waiting staff.
explanation.walkthrough: A tipstaff was a court officer who carried a metal-tipped staff; the word survives as a historical title.
explanation.definitionFit: A tipstaff was a sheriff's or court officer of former times, hence an old officer.

clue.text: Period fixed for something to be learnt in maths

explanation.definitionFit: Michelangelo painted his Last Judgment fresco on the altar wall of the Vatican's famous papal chapel.

clue.text: Stop and wave, passing a slow vehicle

clue.text: Prudence's family in saga on radio

clue.text: Information about people watching sailors
